---
title: "Static discrete choice"
description: "Binary links, multinomial normalization, and low-rank preference matrices."
---

## Random utility and probability normalization

A binary model observes $Y_i=1\{X_i'\beta+\varepsilon_i>0\}$.
Logistic errors give $P_i=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(X_i'\beta)$; standard
normal errors give $P_i=\Phi(X_i'\beta)$. Their coefficient scales differ
because the latent error variances are normalized differently. Compare
probabilities or marginal effects, not raw logit and probit coefficients.

Trex exposes `BinaryLogit` and `BinaryProbit` in `trex.choice`. The
regression-family `LogisticRegression` additionally supports the fixed-effect
and offset machinery described in [GLMs](likelihood-glms.qmd).

For $J$ alternatives, the multinomial model is

$$
P(Y_i=j\mid X_i)=\frac{\exp(X_i'\beta_j)}
{\sum_{k=1}^{J}\exp(X_i'\beta_k)},\qquad \beta_J=0.
$$

The **last alternative** is Trex's reference category. `X` has shape $(n,p)$,
with the same observation-level covariates entering alternative-specific
coefficient vectors. This is not a long-format conditional-logit formula API
for arbitrary alternative-specific covariates.

## Worked example: three alternatives

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from trex.choice import MultinomialLogit

torch.set_num_threads(1)
rng = np.random.default_rng(351)
n = 1200
x = rng.normal(size=n)
X = np.c_[np.ones(n), x]
beta = np.array([[0.3, -0.2], [1.0, -0.8]])
logits = np.c_[X @ beta, np.zeros(n)]
prob = np.exp(logits-logits.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))
prob /= prob.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
choices = np.array([rng.choice(3, p=p) for p in prob])
y = np.eye(3)[choices]  # MultinomialLogit expects one-hot outcomes.
fit = MultinomialLogit(maxiter=150, tol=1e-9, device="cpu").fit(
    torch.tensor(X), torch.tensor(y)
)
pd.DataFrame(fit.params["coef"].detach().numpy(),
             index=["Intercept", "x"], columns=["Alternative 0", "Alternative 1"]).round(3)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-multinomial-probabilities
#| fig-cap: "Fitted probabilities sum to one and vary jointly with the covariate."
grid = np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 160)
pred = fit.predict_proba(torch.tensor(np.c_[np.ones(len(grid)), grid])).detach().numpy()
assert np.allclose(pred.sum(axis=1), 1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for j in range(3):
    ax.plot(grid, pred[:, j], label=f"Alternative {j}")
ax.set(xlabel="x", ylabel="Choice probability", ylim=(0, 1)); ax.legend(); plt.show()
print("Covariance dimensions:", tuple(fit.params["vcov"].shape))
```

The covariance corresponds to the free, non-reference coefficients.
For a covariate $x_k$, the probability derivative is
$\partial P_j/\partial x_k=P_j(\beta_{kj}-\sum_\ell P_\ell\beta_{k\ell})$.
A positive utility coefficient need not mean every comparison of average
probabilities increases: the entire choice set and covariate distribution matter.

## Low-rank preferences over assortments

When users and products repeat, `LowRankLogit` replaces an unrestricted utility
matrix by $\Theta=AB'$, with low-dimensional user and item factors. For a
displayed assortment $S_i$,

$$
P(j\mid u_i,S_i)=\frac{\exp(\Theta_{u_i j})}
{\sum_{k\in S_i}\exp(\Theta_{u_i k})},\quad j\in S_i.
$$

An assortment is part of the conditioning information: an unavailable item is
not an observed rejection. The factors are not separately identified under
rotations. The rank and penalty regularize predictions, not automatically
economic preference parameters. Below is a small full-assortment fit.

```{python}
from trex.choice import LowRankLogit

torch.manual_seed(13)
n_users, n_items, n_obs = 20, 6, 300
users = torch.randint(n_users, (n_obs,))
utility = torch.randn(n_users, 2) @ torch.randn(2, n_items) * 0.4
items = torch.multinomial(torch.softmax(utility[users], dim=1), 1).squeeze(1)
low_rank = LowRankLogit(rank=2, n_users=n_users, n_items=n_items,
                       lam=0.02, maxiter=80, device="cpu")
low_rank.fit(users, items)
print("Full-assortment probabilities for user 0:")
print(low_rank.predict_proba(torch.tensor([0])).detach().numpy().round(3))
```

## Interpretation and checks

Report held-out log loss as well as classification accuracy. Check rare
alternatives and separation; finite optimization does not establish a finite
MLE. Multinomial logit imposes IIA conditional on included covariates; low-rank
heterogeneity changes the model but does not eliminate all substitution
restrictions. Neither fitting choices nor changing covariates identifies price
elasticities without an exogeneity or identification argument.

Low-rank standard errors are not implemented. The static `counterfactual`
helpers compare fitted probabilities; they do not solve a supply equilibrium.

**API:** [BinaryLogit](../reference/choice.BinaryLogit.qmd),
[BinaryProbit](../reference/choice.BinaryProbit.qmd),
[MultinomialLogit](../reference/choice.MultinomialLogit.qmd),
[LowRankLogit](../reference/choice.LowRankLogit.qmd).
